question: According to the International Court of Justice (ICJ) interim ruling on the Application of the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide in Gaza (South Africa v. Israel), Israel must do all it can to prevent death, destruction and any acts of genocide1 in Gaza.
Given that an immediate permanent ceasefire in Gaza is the only way to prevent further death and destruction, it is imperative that a ceasefire is reached.

Considering the EU and Israel Association Agreement2, Article 2 of which states ‘Relations between the Parties, as well as all the provisions of the Agreement itself, shall be based on respect for human rights and democratic principles, which guides their internal and international policy and constitutes an essential element of this Agreement,’ in light of the unfolding humanitarian situation, and taking the ICJ ruling into consideration, will the Commission: 1.
Demand an immediate and sustained ceasefire in Gaza and Israel, in order to protect civilians on all sides?
Suspend or threaten to suspend the EU-Israel Association agreement in order to apply pressure to act in line with the ICJ ruling?
Consider imposing travel restrictions on high-ranking Israeli officials until a ceasefire is reached?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (30.4.2024) As stated in the joint statement by the High Representative/Vice-President and the Commission on 26 January 2024, orders of the International Court of Justice are binding on the Parties and they must comply with them. The EU expects their full, immediate and effective implementation1.

The EU consistently underlines the importance of ensuring the protection of all civilians at all times in line with international humanitarian law. The EU has been consistently calling for extended humanitarian pauses. The EU continues to pass these messages in its statements2 as well as bilaterally in its contacts with the Israeli authorities.

The Foreign Affairs Council had an orientation debate on 18 March 2024 regarding the question of the EU-Israel Association Agreement, which is based on shared values, including the respect for human rights. The Council agreed to continue following this question closely and to invite the Foreign Minister of Israel for a discussion on this matter. The EU is not considering restrictive measures on Israeli officials.
1 International Court of Justice: Joint Statement by the High Representative and the European Commission
